I've been hunkering down lately for the most part. I hadn't been to the grocery store (ShopRite) in a couple of weeks. Last time I was there, everything was normal. I went there this morning, around 8AM. We got a little snow this morning, so I figured I'd take the opportunity to go out while things might be a little more quiet than they otherwise would be. Roads were completely clear. For additional background, there have been very few cases of KungFlu near me - last I knew there was only 1 or 2 in the county. Could be more by now, but nothing overwhelming.

First thing that jumped out at me is they have some sort of testing facility near where I was going. They have the digital highway signs indicating a test facility, "by appt only". There were orange cones at the entrance. Might have been a drive-thru. This was at an old IBM complex that hasn't been fully rented in quite some time.

I stopped at a local convenience store first, good one, normally has good coffee and pastries, bread, milk, so forth. This place is normally slammed at this time of morning. Including me, there were only 2 people in the store...dead. I wasn't there for any of that stuff, so I didn't really look at their supplies, but the place didn't look barren by any means (aside from clientele).

Traffic was dead. There was traffic, but much less than normal.

What was most eerie was empty parking lots in stores that are shut down, deemed non-essential. It looks bizare.

On to the grocery store...to be brief, most things were well stocked. The store was busy with staff restocking the shelves. My first walkthrough, the meats were in rough shape. Ground beef and beef in general was pretty non existent. I found some frozen burgers down the way and threw them in the cart and continued on...I know, but you got to do what you've got to do. Plenty of pork on the shelves. I didn't look through the chicken, but I'm guessing there was plenty, based on a quick look down those cases.

I was treating this as a "normal" shopping trip, I'm not panic buying. Anyway, pasta shelves were pretty thin, but I was able to get my desired pasta, Linguine (Barilla, not my regular brand), and some jarred sauce. Rice - In stock. Butter, eggs, bagels, bacon, Kaiser rolls and other normal bakery goods, in stock. Tons of cookie baskets, WTF?

I didn't bother even looking for toilet paper or paper towels because I didn't need any this time around. I couldn't bring myself to even look.

Anyway, I continued on, checking down my list and pretty much got everything that I wanted. Since they were still stocking shelves, I figured I'd make another pass by the fresh meats, and this time they were stocking the shelves with ground beef, which I grabbed.

At the checkout I was chatting with the cashier. Apparently what they're doing is allowing senior citizens to shop between 7am and 8am before anyone else. She said that there have been a lot of seniors there during that timeframe, wiping out the shelves to the point where they have to restock.

This is all somewhat mindblowing to me. It occurs to me that it's the same as the pre-snowstorm panic buying that goes on. They hype the shit out of snowstorms on TV and people act like armageddon is coming. This is the same mentality.

Anyway, figured I'd pass on the info for anyone interested. Good luck to everyone out there and God bless.
